clauses.text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws
of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform
Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq., it is hereby ordered that:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Subject to the provisions of section 3 of this order, the officers
named in section 2, in the order listed, shall act as, and perform the
duties of, the office of Secretary of State (Secretary) during any period
in which the Secretary has died, resigned, or otherwise become unable
to perform the functions and duties of the office of Secretary.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text: Sec. 2. Order of Succession.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) Deputy Secretary of State;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) Deputy Secretary of State for Management and Resources;

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Under Secretary of State designated for political affairs pursuant to
section 2651a(b) of title 22, United States Code;

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) Under Secretary of State designated for management affairs pursuant
to section 2651a(b) of title 22, United States Code;

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) The remaining Under Secretaries of State, in the order in which they
shall have taken the oath of office as such;

clauses.label: (f)
(g)
clauses.text:
(g) The following officers, in the order in which they shall have taken
the oath of office as such:
(1) Remaining Assistant Secretaries of State;
(2) Coordinator for Counterterrorism;
(3) Director General of the Foreign Service; and
(4) Legal Adviser;

clauses.label: (h)
clauses.text: (h) United States Representative to the United Nations (New York);

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text: (i) Deputy United States Representative to the United Nations (New York);

clauses.label: (j)
clauses.text:
(j) The following other United States Representatives to the United Nations
(New York), in the order in which they shall have taken the oath of office
as such:

(1) United States Representative to the United Nations for United Nations
Management and Reform;

(2) United States Representative to the United Nations on the Economic
and Social Council of the United Nations; and

(3) Alternate United States Representative to the United Nations for
Special Political Affairs in the United Nations;

clauses.label: (k)
clauses.text: (k) The following Chiefs of Mission, in the order listed:
(1) United States Ambassador to the United Kingdom;
(2) United States Ambassador to Canada;

(3) United States Ambassador to Australia;

(5) United States Ambassador to Japan; and

clauses.label: (l)
clauses.text:
(l) The following officers, in the order in which they shall have taken
the oath of office as such:
(1) United States Ambassadors at Large;
(2) Counselor; and
(3) Special Representatives of the President; and

(m) The remaining Chiefs of Mission, in the order in which they shall

clauses.label: Sec. 3.

clauses.label: (a)

(a) No individual who has not been appointed by the President by and

in an acting capacity shall act as Secretary pursuant to this order.

in section 2 for purposes of this order.

clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Executive Order 12343 of January 27, 1982, is hereby revoked.
W

Executive Order 13251 of December 28, 2001
Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of
State
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws
of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform
Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq., it is hereby ordered that:
Section 1. Subject to the provisions of section 3 of this order, the officers
named in section 2, in the order listed, shall act as, and perform the
duties of, the office of Secretary of State (Secretary) during any period
in which the Secretary has died, resigned, or otherwise become unable
to perform the functions and duties of the office of Secretary.
Sec. 2. Order of Succession.
(a) Deputy Secretary of State;
(b) Deputy Secretary of State for Management and Resources;
(c) Under Secretary of State designated for political affairs pursuant to
section 2651a(b) of title 22, United States Code;
(d) Under Secretary of State designated for management affairs pursuant
to section 2651a(b) of title 22, United States Code;
(e) The remaining Under Secretaries of State, in the order in which they
shall have taken the oath of office as such;
(f) Assistant Secretaries of State designated for regional bureaus pursuant
to section 2651a(c) of title 22, United States Code, in the order in which
they shall have taken the oath of office as such;
(g) The following officers, in the order in which they shall have taken
the oath of office as such:
(1) Remaining Assistant Secretaries of State;
(2) Coordinator for Counterterrorism;
(3) Director General of the Foreign Service; and
(4) Legal Adviser;
(h) United States Representative to the United Nations (New York);
(i) Deputy United States Representative to the United Nations (New York);
(j) The following other United States Representatives to the United Nations
(New York), in the order in which they shall have taken the oath of office
as such:
(1) United States Representative to the United Nations for United Nations
Management and Reform;
(2) United States Representative to the United Nations on the Economic
and Social Council of the United Nations; and
(3) Alternate United States Representative to the United Nations for
Special Political Affairs in the United Nations;
(k) The following Chiefs of Mission, in the order listed:
(1) United States Ambassador to the United Kingdom;
(2) United States Ambassador to Canada;
(3) United States Ambassador to Australia;

(4) United States Ambassador to Mexico;
(5) United States Ambassador to Japan; and
(6) United States Ambassador to India;
(l) The following officers, in the order in which they shall have taken
the oath of office as such:
(1) United States Ambassadors at Large;
(2) Counselor; and
(3) Special Representatives of the President; and
(m) The remaining Chiefs of Mission, in the order in which they shall
have taken the oath of office as such.
Sec. 3. Exceptions.
(a) No individual who has not been appointed by the President by and
with the consent of the Senate shall act as Secretary pursuant to this order.
(b) No individual who is serving in an office listed in section 2(a)-(m)
in an acting capacity shall act as Secretary pursuant to this order.
(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains
discretion, to the extent permitted by the Federal Vacancies Reform Act
of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq ., to depart from this order in designating
an acting Secretary.
(d) A successor office, intended to be the equivalent of an office identified
in section 2 of this order, shall be deemed to be the position identified
in section 2 for purposes of this order.
Sec. 4. Executive Order 12343 of January 27, 1982, is hereby revoked.
W

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 13251 (signed 2001-12-28; 67 FR 1599; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13251.txt, read in full) prescribes the order in which officers of the Department of State act as Secretary of State when the Secretary cannot serve, states exceptions, and revokes Executive Order 12343. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 13251 of December 28, 2001, on an order of succession within the Department of State at 67 FR 1599, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has thirty-eight clauses, four of which are too short to verify as quotations, so I replaced it with nineteen clauses (inventory override): the authority recital, section 1, the paragraphs of section 2 (with numbered subparagraphs joined to their parent paragraphs and the heading joined to paragraphs (a) and (b)), the paragraphs of section 3 and section 4. Own terms: no clause of sections 1 to 3 has an end date or ending condition; section 4 is a self-executing revocation of EO 12343 performed on issuance and recorded as terminated on 2001-12-28; section 3(b) was replaced by EO 13261. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 13251 finds EO 13261 (replacing section 3(b), attached as a later event), the order's own Federal Register copy and a 2010 Federal Register document whose authority line reads Executive Order 13251 dated November 24, 2009, which is a miscitation of another order and not an instrument affecting this one; no held text revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 1 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held amendment and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of 22 U.S.C. 2651a and of the Vacancies Act as now codified is not held, and the held evidence does not show whether any listed office was renamed or abolished (section 3(d) deems a successor office to be the position).

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 13251 (signed 2001-12-28; 67 FR 1599; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13251.txt, read in full) prescribes the order in which officers of the Department of State act as Secretary of State when the Secretary cannot serve, states exceptions, and revokes Executive Order 12343. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 13251 of December 28, 2001, on an order of succession within the Department of State at 67 FR 1599, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has thirty-eight clauses (the lead-in, sections 1 to 4 and their lettered and numbered paragraphs); I confirmed it without correction. Own terms: no clause of sections 1 to 3 has an end date or ending condition; section 4 is a self-executing revocation of EO 12343 performed on issuance and recorded as terminated on 2001-12-28; section 3(b) was replaced by EO 13261. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 13251 finds EO 13261 (replacing section 3(b), attached as a later event), the order's own Federal Register copy and a 2010 Federal Register document whose authority line reads Executive Order 13251 dated November 24, 2009, which is a miscitation of another order and not an instrument affecting this one; no held text revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 1 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held amendment and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of 22 U.S.C. 2651a and of the Vacancies Act as now codified is not held, and the held evidence does not show whether any listed office was renamed or abolished (section 3(d) deems a successor office to be the position).
